thread:
maria: Ran an nsys + perfetto slice against the 7B continuous-batch workload on ded-dev today. Seeing a weird pattern: many tiny cuBLASLt matmuls with repeated algo-probe calls and per-call workspace alloc/free in the timeline. launch-overhead + workspace churn look like the biggest contributors to tail.

kevin: can you paste the top-line numbers?

maria: quick paste from the nsys summary: 
```
Total kernel time: 2.3s
# matmul (cublasLt) calls: 3,420
avg matmul runtime: 640us (stdev 210us)
avg kernel launch overhead measured in timeline: 45-60us per call
Workspace alloc/free syscalls spiked right before matmul in many slices (~12us each)
KV-cache fill spikes at token 0-10, correlates with extra matmul calls
```

anya: :eyes: that launch overhead is high for small shapes. are we falling back to an algo-probe path every time because workspace not big enough?

maria: exactly my hunch. perfetto flame shows cublasLt::AlgoSearch entries interleaved with matmul calls. Looks like we probe at a per-shape granularity when we hit a new seqlen in a batch.

sam: is this the run with dynamic batching (mixed seqlen) enabled? we saw probe storms when batching mixes 8/16/32.

maria: yes dynamic batching ON, batch windows ~50ms. when multiple seq lengths hit same device slice, the runtime requests cuBLASLt algos for each (and sometimes re-probes because the selected algo needs a larger workspace than currently reserved).

kevin: can you share the nsight timeline snapshot (frame id)? I want to look at kernel host-side latency and mem allocs.

maria: uploaded qdrep -> //redwood-shared/nsys/run_1939876543.qdrep and perfetto trace -> //redwood-shared/perfetto/run_1939876543.pb. Key screenshot: timeline shows pattern: [host alloc] -> [cublasLt::AlgoSearch] (20-30us) -> [alloc workspace] -> [matmul kernel] -> [free workspace]. repeated.

perf-bot: perf-regression-checker detected +18% p99 tail on token latency vs baseline (190s baseline window). Regression tag: matmul-ws-spill-1939876543.

anya: short term mitigation ideas: 1) pre-allocate per-stream workspace slab keyed by model/seqbucket and reuse, 2) cache algo selection by (shape, dtype, quantization) in-memory with TTL longer than batch window, 3) force a single chosen algo with fallback path (avoid per-request probing).

maria: tried option 1 locally: prealloc slab reduces alloc/free spikes but still seeing algo-probe calls because cuBLASLt API returns CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED for current workspace size then we increase — that causes a probe loop. caching result of 'best algo for workspace X' helped.

sam: we should also check our cublasLt setOperation/Preference flags. If we set CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG to prefer fast-launch algos and clamp workspace min to what slab offers, we can avoid repeated re-probes.

kevin: follow-up action: can we run a micro-benchmark to reproduce outside RL? i.e., iterate shapes seen in trace (seq 8/16/32) with our allocator and measure algoselection churn. I'll spin one up.

maria: created job ded-dev:matmul-warmup-193987 on k8s (pod: ded-matmul-probe-193987). logs -> //redwood-logs/ded-matmul-probe-193987.log. Early run shows probe calls drop by ~80% when we prewarm the algo cache at startup.

infra-bot: deployment note: ded-dev has CUDA 11.8 / cuBLASLt 1.1 pinned for this run.

anya: another angle: KV-cache warmup at token 0-10 causes many small unique matmuls (different prefix shapes), so we hit many shape variants quickly. Could smooth this by staged KV warmup or by issuing a small synthetic warmup batch that exercises common seq buckets at connection start.

maria: tried synthetic warmup (batch of 64 tokens across common buckets) — reduced first-token latency by ~30% in experiments. downside: extra cost on cold starts.

kevin: longer term: add a compact algo-cache keyed by model_id + shape_hash in the runtime control plane; populate during model load and keep persisted across restarts. TTL per model version.

sam: agree. also add telemetry: count algo-probe events per minute per tenant so we can alert on unusually high probe rates.

maria: summary/actions: 
- small reproducer job running (ded-matmul-probe-193987) -> perf artifacts uploaded
- short-term: prewarm algo cache + slab workspace prealloc (opt-in flag) tested, promising
- mid-term: persistent algo cache + telemetry + prefer-fast-algo tuning
- mitigation: synthetic warmup on cold start for high-throughput customers

kevin: assigning ticket RNF-2318 to implement persistent algo cache. I'll pick up telemetry + alerting.

anya: I'll prototype the slab allocator tweak and add a feature flag.

maria: thanks all. next step: merge micro-benchmark results into the runtime PR and run full-suite regression. tagging @eng-sre to watch rollout. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: rerun baseline after PR to confirm p99 back to target.

infra-bot: snapshot saved: image-redwood/ded-matmul:2026-03-18-1939

kevin: closing loop — will post updated perf graphs when we have PR numbers.

sam: nice catch, good repro path.

maria: attaching minimal perf snippet for reference: 
```c++
// pseudo: probe cache warmstart
for (auto shape : common_shapes) {
  auto pref = buildPreference(workspace_size);
  cublasLtMatmul(..., pref, &algo); // run once to populate cache
}
```

maria: end of thread.
